title: Ten-MHz peak changes can reverse a fixed-range order contrast in 33 selected CHIME events
abstract: We test the effect of bounded peak-frequency errors on a published component-order result in CHIME/FRB Catalog 2 release 20251231. We keep time order, component count and original frequency-range weights fixed. For 33 events from 20 source labels, the contrast between the exact internal-shuffle mean path and the observed path is 0.29766 at the reported peaks. Mixed-integer linear programs give a minimum of 0.14001 when each peak can change independently by at most 5 MHz. At 10 MHz, a feasible set of changes gives -0.02566. The sign is thus protected at 5 MHz but can reverse at 10 MHz under these error boxes. At 5 MHz the 95 percent source-resample interval is -0.02349 to 0.31596. The interior-peak subset retains a positive sample bound at 10 MHz. These bounds do not estimate actual peak errors, recompute the earlier shuffle probability, or establish an instrument cause. Peak covariance, selection and time-order errors are not modeled. No independent telescope data confirm this test and no new source is found. Code, aggregate evidence, source hashes and separate-scratch reproduction steps are included.

display.caption: Smallest allowed fixed-range contrast as the bound on each peak change grows. The band shows source-resample variation for the main sample. It is not a peak-error confidence interval.
